_: P-PROC-06's allowlist: modules that compute no number reaching score, route or tags, so CLAUDE.md's 'a new numeric module ships its mutation population' does not apply. ONE REASON PER ENTRY, read from the module. ops/lib/check-mutate-population.py refuses an empty reason, an entry for a module a population also covers, and an entry naming a file that does not exist. It cannot tell numeric from non-numeric - that is a reading, recorded in T-0186's Log and re-read by a reviewer on every widening of this file.

modules.services/etl/etl/byway_source.py: parses the two byway pulls into the entry shape byways.match consumes; shapes records, computes nothing
modules.services/etl/etl/checkbounds.py: compares a built extract's meta.json with region.json and never builds; its numbers gate a build, they reach no score, route or tag
modules.services/etl/etl/contentdigest.py: a sha256 over what the corpus says; a digest of bytes, not a quantity
modules.services/etl/etl/corpus.py: the `python -m etl.corpus` command line; wiring over corpuswriter and the producers
modules.services/etl/etl/corpuswriter.py: writes corpus.sqlite deterministically; it stores the numbers others computed
modules.services/etl/etl/counts.py: per-class object counts out of osmium fileinfo; the bounds make a silent drop loud and stop there
modules.services/etl/etl/extract.py: drives osmium to cut the region and filter tags; a subprocess pipeline
modules.services/etl/etl/extractway.py: reads the committed JSON extract into ExtractWay rows
modules.services/etl/etl/fetch.py: fetches the manifest's inputs and verifies every byte; no arithmetic leaves it
modules.services/etl/etl/manifest.py: the table of external inputs, their verification mode and their licence
modules.services/etl/etl/oracle.py: builds the Curvature oracle fixture from somebody else's published output; the oracle is the CHECK on a number, not a number we ship
modules.services/etl/etl/oracle_report.py: reports the oracle's agreement figures with the platform that produced them; a report, consumed by humans
modules.services/etl/etl/oracle_select.py: the three conditions deciding which oracle ways are comparable; selection, not measurement
modules.services/etl/etl/osmxml.py: a stream copy between `osmium cat` and the tag pass (T-0168's closing ruling, quoted in ops/mutate/scenic_tags.py)
modules.services/etl/etl/region.py: a region is a bbox, a name and the recorded shape of the last extract
modules.services/etl/etl/review_sheet.py: renders a page of Street View links with a verdict control for a human
modules.services/etl/etl/schema.py: the corpus DDL and SCHEMA_VERSION; the version that would matter is already pinned by P-PROD-05 (ops/lib/check-schema-version.py)
modules.services/etl/etl/streetview.py: turns coordinates and a heading into a URL a human clicks
modules.services/etl/etl/tagfilter.py: the osmium tags-filter expressions the extract keeps
modules.services/etl/etl/terms.py: the term vocabulary - ids, ODbL family, producer - the on-device score contract as data
modules.services/etl/etl/waydoc.py: wiring over producers that carry their own numbers (T-0168's closing ruling, quoted in ops/mutate/scenic_tags.py)
modules.Sources/ScenicKit/Model/Coordinate.swift: a WGS-84 latitude/longitude pair; Foundation-only so ScenicKit builds on Linux
modules.Sources/ScenicKit/Scoring/BywayTier.swif: a three-state enum naming how a way is designated; the weight that uses it lives in SegmentTerms.swift, which ops/mutate/segmentscore.py covers
modules.Sources/ScenicKit/Guidance/GuidanceManeu: the maneuver vocabulary as an enum; the mapping that assigns it is GuidanceMapping.swift, which ops/mutate/guidance.py covers
